disagreements.topic: FY2028 EPS growth (sets Oct-2027 NTM EPS, the main input to every P/E leg)
disagreements.positions: agent_3 +12% ($24.56, tied to GS's ~12% 2028 hyperscaler capex growth); agent_5 +15% ($25.2); agent_4 +17% ($26.0); agent_1 +18% ($25.9); agent_2 +18.5% ($26.0). So NTM EPS ranges from $23.9 to $25.1, about +/-$12 per ADR at 19x.
disagreements.resolution: Not settled. No free source gives a FY2028 consensus (stockanalysis keeps 2027-28 behind a paywall, and Alpha Vantage stops at FY2027). The FY2027 consensus range is already $19.58-$24.62 across 13 analysts (+/-12%), so the FY28 spread between agents is inside normal estimate noise. I use a central +15-16% (NTM ~$24.6-24.8) and do not move the ladder for it.
disagreements.evidence: Alpha Vantage EARNINGS_ESTIMATES, Oct 2, 2026 (FY27 avg $21.93, high $24.62, low $19.58, 13 analysts, 9 up/0 down in 30d; FY26 $16.93); stockanalysis.com forecast page (2027-28 restricted).

disagreements.positions: agent_3 18.5x NTM; agents 4/5 19x; agents 1/2 19.5x (agent_2 adds 21x on FY27). Implied fair values $418 (agent_3) to $473 (agent_2).
disagreements.resolution: Rate facts verified at the primary source. The 10-year closed at 5.29% on Sep 30 and 5.24% on Oct 1, 2026, with the 3-month bill at 4.17%. A 19-19.5x multiple is an earnings yield of ~5.1-5.3%, about level with the 10-year. Today's 20.9x on FY27 already carries that, and estimates are still being raised. That supports the 19-19.5x middle. Agent_3's 18.5x on top of a 3% EPS haircut stacks two bearish judgments; it is a valid skeptic view, but no checked fact requires it.
disagreements.evidence: US Treasury daily par yield curve CSV 2026 (10y 5.29% Sep 30, 5.24% Oct 1; 3m 4.17% Oct 1).

disagreements.topic: How unusual the yield level is (a factual conflict between agents)
disagreements.positions: agents 2 and 3: '5.29%, highest since 2007'. agents 1, 4, 5: 'highest since 2002' (agent_4 cites a 5.33% intraday print).
disagreements.resolution: Agents 1, 4 and 5 are right on closing levels. The Sep 30 close of 5.29% is above the 2007 peak (5.26%, Jun 12, 2007) and the 2006 peak (5.25%, Jun 28, 2006), so it is the highest close since 2002. 5.33% was intraday only. The valuation effect is negligible, but agents 2 and 3 should fix the label.
disagreements.evidence: US Treasury daily par yield curve CSVs for 2006, 2007 and 2026.

disagreements.positions: agents 1/4 $85B, agent_2 $88B (2027) and $105B (2028), agent_3 $90B/$105B. OCF margin: agent_3 63.5%, agent_4 65%. FCF legs: agent_1 DCF $353, agent_3 $393, agent_4 $432, agent_2 $446.
disagreements.resolution: Round-2 inputs are close: $85-90B covers BofA and UBS. The UBS figures still come only from one Substack recap; BofA's $85B is a separate source that confirms the direction. A $5B change in capex moves FY27 FCF by ~$1/ADR and blended fair values by only ~$3-8, because every agent now weights FCF at 0.15-0.3. Agent_1's 5-year DCF with a 4% terminal is structurally low for a business growing ~18%, which agent_1 itself notes, so its $353 should not be read as a downside anchor.
disagreements.evidence: Round-1 supervisor checks (404K Research recap of UBS, Sep 28; Startup Fortune on BofA $85B); agent files.

disagreements.positions: agents 1/2: the Fed 'signalled one more hike' (dot plot). agent_5: Kalshi ~66% hold / 34% hike for Oct 28.
disagreements.resolution: The two are consistent: one more 2026 hike could come in December. FOMC Oct 27-28 is on the Fed's 2026 calendar. Agent_5 reports the Kalshi figure from secondary trackers (the page returned 403), so it is colour, not a driver. Nobody makes a strong directional 1-month call, and I agree.
disagreements.evidence: Federal Reserve 2026 FOMC calendar; agent_5 notes.

disagreements.positions: Agent fair values average ~$452 (418-473), but lognormal medians sit at $462-483, i.e. +$10-25 for estimate momentum.
disagreements.resolution: The drift is reasonable. FY27 consensus rose from $19.66 to $21.93 in 90 days (+11.5%) with 9 up / 0 down in 30 days, and FY26 from $15.77 to $16.93. A median ~$470-475 against a ~$455 fair value is consistent with that. I left the mean ladder unchanged.

one_month_reasoning: Sep revenue on Oct 8, Q3 results and Q4 guide on Oct 15, and the FOMC on Oct 27-28 all fall in the window. The beat is expected (Jul+Aug NT$982B; Q3 consensus EPS $4.46 vs Q4 $4.97), the swing factors are Q4 GM and 2027 capex framing, and a 10-year near its highest close since 2002 roughly offsets the usual post-beat drift. The five agents agree within 1-2 points, so I keep their mean: median ~+0.5%, ~12% monthly sigma.
confidence_reason: Round 2 has converged: P(>=459) ranges only 0.487-0.536 across agents, and the remaining disputes (FY28 growth, 18.5x vs 19.5x) could not be settled with a primary source. My checks verified rates and the FY27 consensus, and they confirm the mean rather than move it. No update beats the mean here.
thesis_break_reason: $330 is ~28% below spot, ~15x the verified $21.93 FY27 consensus and ~13.4x Oct-2027 NTM EPS, near the March 2026 lows ($314-338). A close there would most likely mean FY27 estimates are being cut (AI order pushouts at the top-2 customers, a GM reset below ~58%) or a Taiwan/Section 232 repricing. A 5.3% 10-year alone explains only ~1-1.5 turns of multiple.
key_drivers: FY27 consensus EPS $21.93/ADR (+30% on FY26 $16.93), revised up from $19.66 in 90 days with 9 up / 0 down; the stock trades at ~20.9x that.
FY28 growth is the biggest open input: agents range +12% to +18.5%, which spans ~$24-25 NTM EPS and ~+/-$12/ADR at 19x; there is no free consensus to settle it.
Rates: the 10-year closed at 5.29% on Sep 30 (highest close since 2002), the 3-month bill is at 4.17%, and the Fed hiked Sep 16. This caps the exit multiple at ~19-19.5x.
Capex steps up to ~$85-90B in 2027 (BofA $85B; UBS $90B via one secondary recap) and ~$105B in 2028, holding FY27 FCF to ~$11-12.5/ADR.
Taiwan/tariff tail: a 4-5% crash state; all agents rely on the same single Polymarket market (13% invasion by end-2027).

fair_value.reason: P/E leg: 19-19.5x Oct-2027 NTM EPS of ~$24.7 (0.25 x FY27 $21.93 + 0.75 x FY28 ~$25.4 at +16%) = ~$470-480. FCF leg: ~$415-430 (FY27-28 FCF ~$11.5-12.5/ADR after $85-90B/$105B capex at a ~2.8-2.9% yield). Weighted ~0.75/0.25, that gives ~$455. It sits slightly above the agents' ~$452 average because agent_1's 5-year DCF ($353, 4% terminal) and agent_3's stacked haircut plus 18.5x look structurally low; no agent made a factual error large enough to move it further.

missed: Its DCF ($353) is a 5-year model with a 4% terminal at a capex peak; agent_1 says itself this is structurally low, but it still carries 0.3 weight and pulls the fair value to $446.
FY28 growth of +18% sits at the top of the group, and no checked consensus supports it (Alpha Vantage stops at FY27, and the FY27 range alone is $19.58-24.62).
feedback_for_agents.revisit: Either lengthen the DCF to a 10-year fade or cut its weight, and show a +15% FY28 sensitivity. The rest (net cash $18.6/ADR from the 2Q26 balance sheet, Oct 8 date, 10y since 2002) is verified and good.

FY28 +18.5% and a 21x current-year leg keep it the most bullish agent; the N2 order +10-20% claim is trade press, not confirmed by TSMC.

It stacks a 3% EPS haircut, an 18.5x multiple and +12% FY28 growth, which is three bearish judgments on the same risk (GM dilution and AI digestion).

summary: The five round-2 forecasts have converged on a ~$470-480 median with a fat left tail: P(>=$459) is 0.49-0.54. My checks verified the rate backdrop (10-year 5.29% close, highest since 2002; T-bill 4.17%) and the rising FY27 consensus ($21.93, 9 up / 0 down). They could not settle the one input still in dispute, FY2028 growth (+12% to +18.5%), so I keep the mean ladder unchanged with low confidence. Fair value is ~$455 (~1% below spot) and the thesis breaks at $330 (~15x FY27): a fully priced quality compounder that is roughly a coin flip to be higher in a year.

sizing.conviction_label_reason: Checked evidence puts fair value (~$455) at spot and the median only ~+3-4%, which is not enough to beat SPY's Sharpe at ~3x SPY's volatility, so there is no checked edge.
sizing.entry: 2 tranches over ~6 weeks: half after the Oct 15 Q3 print/Q4 guide, half after Nvidia's late-November results
sizing.overlap: AVGO (AI accelerator/ASIC demand, a TSMC customer), GOOGL (hyperscaler AI capex, TPUs made at TSMC), VST (AI build-out via power); ~14% of the portfolio already rides AI capex
sizing.reason: TSM is a very liquid mega-cap with no listing or lock-up risk, but it is roughly fairly priced after a ~59% 1-year run and adds to an existing AI-capex concentration. With realized vol near 40% vs ~11% for SPY and a 4.17% T-bill hurdle, it needs a ~+15-16% return to match an ~8% SPY year on Sharpe; my ladder gives that about a 35-40% chance, partly offset by down-market states where its volatility-scaled loss is smaller. Earnings (Oct 15), the 5%+ rate backdrop and the Taiwan tail argue for a cap of ~4%.
